most creative strategists throw around the word "format" without actually understanding what it means. they say "podcast ad" or "monk ad" or "Pixar song ad" — but they're mixing up structures, conceits, actors, and styles without realizing it.
after generating over $100M+ in sales, these are the 16 ad formats I see running across every top account right now. if you master these, you can cover the 90/10 of winning ads — and if you're missing any of them, they could be the missing links keeping your ad account from scaling.
this video breaks down the complete "ad DNA" system for understanding, analyzing, and stacking ad formats — plus a full walkthrough of all 16 god-tier formats with real examples.
in this video, you'll discover:
⚡ what an "ad format" actually means (and why most people use the term wrong)
 ⚡ the ad DNA framework: skeleton (structure) × CAS (conceit, actor, style, terrain, setup)
 ⚡ why these elements multiply together — and how stacking them unlocks unlimited creative ideas
 ⚡ why better "ad grammar" gives you the ability to detect patterns, find gaps, and generate new winners
 ⚡ the 16 god-tier ad formats running across every major ad account right now
 ⚡ story ads: the 8 subtypes that work (revenge, events, interrogation, and more)
 ⚡ timeline ads: why they're one of the most unbeatable ad structures ever discovered
 ⚡ skeleton ads: the study of memetics and why certain visual symbols capture human attention
 ⚡ product-aware / most-aware ads: ironic reversals, offer-based hooks, and comparison formats
 ⚡ microdrama ads: why AI just hit an inflection point and the runway for innovation is massive
 ⚡ Pixar song ads: rules of thumb for rhyming, music, editing, and storytelling
 ⚡ claymation ads: why this style is perfect for mechanism-based creative
 ⚡ long-form static ads: the narrative format mastered by brands like Rosabella
 ⚡ authority ads: monks, doctors, Dr. Pickle — and why there's way more creativity left to explore
 ⚡ personification ads: how to personify problems, culprits, victims, solutions, products, and ingredients (plus ensemble casts)
 ⚡ monster ads: why weird creatures, mummies, and Frankensteins grab attention
 ⚡ facet demo ads: how to slice your market by habits, traits, and identity for hyper-specific targeting
 ⚡ pretty girl ads, gay spokesperson ads, animal & baby ads, and listicle ads
 ⚡ how to stack formats together (timeline + podcast + monk + Pixar + singing + skeleton) to create ideas that feel like child's play
 ⚡ why ridiculousness is winning right now — and why you should do more of it
